summary: AC-1 is met. A fresh copy installed from the lockfile builds with Vite and the QA app serves the same bundle (index-Dlz99EAX.js), in which React draws the Ada trial heading (TC-1). The sources are TypeScript React components built by Vite (TC-2, with a person's reading still to do). The project's unit run passes 2 of 2 Vitest tests (TC-3) and its browser run passes 1 of 1 Playwright test in Chromium (TC-4). A type error stops the build with TS2322 (TC-5). No defect. Seven added checks pass; three of them prove low findings from Code review.

criteria.note: Every designed test passed on its last run. TC-2 also carries a manual step: a person reads src/App.tsx and src/main.tsx, attached to its result.

findings.title: The unit run warns that an update to Root was not wrapped in act
findings.experience: a React act warning from the main entry test whenever the run shows console output (verbose or JSON reporter); the default reporter hides it
findings.on_user_path: yes, for anyone running Vitest verbose or with a JSON report
findings.cause: src/App.test.tsx main entry test mounts the app through main.tsx outside act and never unmounts that root (Code review, line 14)
findings.confirmed_by: ad hoc: 3 default runs printed 0 warnings, 3 JSON-reporter runs and 2 verbose runs each printed 1; TC-3's attached output shows it too

findings.title: The browser tests build the app again after CI has built it
findings.experience: every CI run builds and type-checks twice, so the browser step is slower
findings.cause: playwright.config.ts line 14 web server runs npm run build; ci.yml line 28 has already built
findings.confirmed_by: TC-7: dist/index.html is written again by npm run test:e2e after npm run build; read in code at ci.yml line 28

findings.title: The unit tests cannot load when packages are installed with npm's legacy peer setting
findings.who: a developer or CI image with legacy-peer-deps set
findings.experience: the unit run fails with Cannot find package @testing-library/dom and runs no tests
findings.on_user_path: no for the default npm ci; yes where legacy-peer-deps is set
findings.cause: package.json does not list @testing-library/dom; the lockfile has it only as a peer (Code review, package.json line 21)
findings.confirmed_by: ad hoc probe and TC-8 both show Test Files 1 failed, Cannot find package @testing-library/dom

findings.title: The coverage status step runs the pull request's own script with a token that can write commit statuses
findings.who: repository owners relying on commit statuses
findings.experience: a same-repository pull request could post any status, such as a passing required check
findings.on_user_path: only for people with push access
findings.cause: ci.yml line 64 runs scripts/patch-coverage.mjs from the pull request checkout with GH_TOKEN (statuses: write) in its env; the comment at line 39 says the job runs nothing untrusted
findings.confirmed_by: read in code only: GitHub Actions cannot run in this environment. Note: on pull_request a same-repository author can also edit ci.yml itself, so this may add little over existing push access; the QA person decides

findings.title: The coverage status job fails on pull requests from forks
findings.experience: a red coverage-status job even when coverage is fine
findings.on_user_path: not today; every pull request comes from a branch in this repository
findings.cause: ci.yml line 68: fork pull requests get a read-only token, so gh api statuses fails

findings.title: The coverage/patch status is reported by the change it measures
findings.experience: a pull request can supply any lcov, so the status is advice, not a control
findings.cause: ci.yml line 36 uploads coverage/lcov.info from the job that runs the pull request's code

findings.title: CI actions are pinned to the movable v4 tag
findings.experience: a moved tag would run new action code next to a statuses: write token
findings.cause: ci.yml line 15 and the coverage-status job

findings.title: The coverage tests in test/coverage are not picked up by the project's own browser test layer
findings.who: the team keeping these coverage tests
findings.experience: npm run test:e2e runs only e2e/, so TC-1, TC-3 and TC-4 run only under Ada's QA config
findings.cause: playwright.config.ts testDir is ./e2e and tsconfig.node.json does not include test/; both are outside this run's paths

findings.title: Two of my own test versions failed on their own assertions
findings.experience: an earlier report of TC-4 and of the added checks file shows two failures each
findings.cause: TC-4 looked for vite build in output Playwright's web server hides; TC-6 expected the act warning from Vitest's default reporter, which hides passing tests' console output. Both fixed once at the cause; the last runs of both files pass
findings.confirmed_by: the project's runs in those attachments passed with exit status 0; ad hoc reporter probe

suggested_follow_ups: Unmount the root the main entry test mounts, or render inside act
Let the Playwright web server skip the build when dist exists in CI, or drop CI's separate build step
Run scripts/patch-coverage.mjs from the base branch in the coverage-status job, pin actions to commit SHAs, and treat coverage/patch as advice
Include test/coverage in the project's Playwright testDir and tsconfig
